stem: A pharmacist compares Syndros oral solution with Marinol capsules. Which statements apply to Syndros? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Its Schedule II prescription may not be refilled.
The Massachusetts 30-day Schedule II validity period applies.
It follows the Schedule III refill rule used for Marinol.
The liquid dosage form makes it Schedule VI.
Syndros is Schedule II although Marinol capsules are Schedule III.

explanation.core_reasoning: The supported conclusions on these facts are: Its Schedule II prescription may not be refilled. The Massachusetts 30-day Schedule II validity period applies. Syndros is Schedule II although Marinol capsules are Schedule III.

choice_analysis.A: Supported: Its Schedule II prescription may not be refilled.
choice_analysis.B: Supported: The Massachusetts 30-day Schedule II validity period applies.
choice_analysis.C: Not supported: It follows the Schedule III refill rule used for Marinol.
choice_analysis.D: Not supported: The liquid dosage form makes it Schedule VI.
choice_analysis.E: Supported: Syndros is Schedule II although Marinol capsules are Schedule III.

related_facts: dronabinol oral solution (Syndros) is used for chemotherapy-associated nausea and vomiting and aids-related anorexia; it is federal Schedule II and Massachusetts Schedule II.
Federal law prohibits refilling a Schedule II prescription; additional dispensing requires a new lawful prescription or a permitted remainder of a partial fill.
A Massachusetts written or electronic Schedule II prescription becomes invalid 30 days after its issue date.
explanation.mpje_trap: Distinguish this near-miss from the controlling rule: 'It follows the Schedule III refill rule used for Marinol.'

reasoning_steps: Classify dronabinol oral solution under the federal and Massachusetts schedules before selecting a legal pathway
Match the scenario's operative facts to Schedule II prescriptions may not be refilled
Reject nearby rules whose schedule, trigger, deadline, or actor differs from Schedule II refills
